steps.name: outside docs needed?
steps.instructions: Do not write the spec and do not ask questions: decide only whether the spec needs facts from outside this repository. Read the request and grep the code it touches (a few files, edit nothing). WEB is yes when the request or that code depends on a third-party API, webhook, library or standard (a protocol, a file format) whose details the criteria need (field names, payload formats, enum values, versions, limits, auth) and the repository does not hold them (no client, DTO, fixture, recorded payload or vendored doc settles them). WEB is no for work inside this code (a refactor, a rename, a page, a rule on data the repository already has), and when the request already carries web research with source URLs (a spike's findings). On yes, list the exact outside facts the criteria need, one per line, with the vendor or library and what the repository already shows (file:line). At most 15 lines. End with exactly one line: WEB: yes, or WEB: no.

steps.name: research the outside docs
steps.instructions:
Research what this feature's spec needs from outside the repository: the third-party APIs, webhooks, libraries or standards the request depends on (field names, payload formats, versions, limits). Search first, then fetch the best sources; never conclude from one failed URL. Edit nothing. What the spec needs from outside, as the explorer found it:
{{data.web_check_text}}

steps.name: interview
steps.instructions:
Interview the person before the spec is written; write no file. Read the request, the evidence handed over (if any), keel's memory of the project and only the code the request names. Go through these lenses: goal and users (who gains what; what "user" means), scope (what is in, what is out), edge cases (absent, empty, malformed, duplicate, limit, a later update, an old message still queued), validation and errors (what is refused, what the caller sees), security (who may read and change what, what must never be logged), data (new fields, migration, existing rows, message contracts), UX (empty, loading and error states), performance (a number, or none), rollout (deploy order between producer and consumer, old clients, feature flag), out of scope. Skip a lens the request, the code or the evidence already answers, or that does not apply. For each lens still open whose answer would change the criteria, ask one question: at most 6, most important first, each with 2 to 4 options (the recommended one first, "recommended": true, each saying what it costs), ending your answer with one ```keel-questions block (a JSON list of {"id", "question", "why", "options": [{"label", "description", "recommended"}]}; the person can also answer in their own words). When nothing is open, ask nothing and end with "NO_QUESTIONS: <why, in one line>". Always write first, in a short list, what each lens already says and where (request, file:line, URL). When the answers come back, write that list again with each answer in it. The web research on the outside docs this feature depends on ("(nothing yet)" when it did not need any): do not ask what it confirmed; ask about what it could not confirm when that would change the criteria.
{{data.web_docs_text}}

steps.name: spec
one explorer per area
steps.instructions: The criteria are settled. Map your area for the criteria in your item: the files each one touches, the pattern to copy (file:line), the test layer and where similar tests live (say so when none do), and the exposures this work inherits (concurrency, idempotency, authorization, data shape). Read only, at most 60 lines, no opinion on architecture, no code. End with MAP-END.

steps.name: plan under the criteria
steps.instructions:
Append a "## Plan" section to the spec (replace the one that is there): the AC order (dependencies first: the criterion that creates a row before the one that reads it), the files per criterion from the maps below, the contract delta (or "none"), and the test layer per criterion (the lowest that can express it). An exposure the maps found that no criterion covers becomes a new criterion now, numbered after the last one. Do not change the other criteria. Under the plan, one line per criterion that needs another one built first: "- AC-n depends on: AC-x, AC-y". ORDER lists the criteria ids in build order. End with CONTRACT-DELTA: yes, or CONTRACT-DELTA: none when the plan's contract delta is none. The explorers' maps:
{{data.report}}

steps.name: the contract delta: new, changed, breaks callers
red
steps.instructions: If the frozen spec is wrong for this criterion (it cannot be true, it contradicts what the code shows, or a criterion is missing), do not work around it: stop and end your answer with one line AMEND: <what the spec says, what the code shows, what should change>. If you cannot go on for another reason (the test command or the build does not work, or another criterion must be built first), end with one line BLOCKED: <tooling, or needs AC-x>: <what>. Otherwise do not write those lines.

steps.name: green
steps.instructions: If the frozen spec turns out to be wrong for this criterion, do not build around it: stop and end your answer with one line AMEND: <what the spec says, what the code shows, what should change>. If you cannot go on for another reason (the test command or the build does not work, or another criterion must be built first), end with one line BLOCKED: <tooling, or needs AC-x>: <what>. Otherwise do not write those lines.

steps.name: refactor (tests frozen)
steps.instructions: This criterion is green. Tidy only the code GREEN just wrote for it and the code it touched: duplication GREEN built up, a name that no longer says what it does, a long function that hides its steps, dead code it left. Behaviour stays exactly the same: the tests are frozen (you cannot edit them) and must stay green. No new behaviour, no new public surface, nothing outside this criterion's code. When nothing is worth tidying, change nothing. End with exactly one line: REFACTOR: done, or REFACTOR: none.

steps.name: integration
steps.instructions: Every criterion is green. Wire the real client to the real API where the criteria's code still uses a stand-in (wiring, not new behaviour; tests are frozen). New behaviour here is a missed criterion: do not write it, say which criterion is missing. When nothing needs wiring, change nothing and say so.

steps.name: the diff for the integration gate
security auditor + dependency triager
steps.instructions: The audit reads the branch diff in your item against the spec's authorization, validation and data rules. The dependency triage judges each advisory in your item: is it reachable from this code? Report findings only.

steps.name: verify the suite + commit the fix
full-diff review
steps.instructions: Read the spec's criteria and scope, then the whole branch diff against the base branch. Go through your whole checklist: correctness across criteria, shared config keys, parameters and routes against the old version, each public type against its contract, a consumer's upgrade, runtime deprecations, the project's CI config (name its commands). Never edit; run only the project's read-only checks. End with a "What I did not check" list.

steps.name: smoke
steps.instructions:
This step writes the smoke checks, not E2E specs: smoke/<feature>.sh (portable bash against BASE_URL and API_URL: health, one critical write, the read of what it wrote) and one @smoke test for the most critical path. Every check seeds its own data, is safe against a deployed environment and runs in under 60 seconds. The checks:
{{data.smoke.checks}}

steps.name: e2e
steps.instructions:
Write one end-to-end test per criterion below, the criterion id in its title, tagged @e2e. Only the e2e folder is writable: a test that needs a UI change to be testable is a [WEB] criterion; stop and say so. {{data.e2e.note}} The criteria:
{{data.e2e.criteria}}

steps.name: docs the change makes wrong
steps.instructions: This step is about the project's own docs, not code and not keel's knowledge base. Read the branch diff against the base branch, then the README, the CHANGELOG (when the project keeps one), the API docs (an OpenAPI description, docs/api, pages for the routes this branch adds or changes) and the user guide pages. Edit only what this change makes wrong or incomplete: a new or changed route, flag, config key, command or behaviour a reader would miss. A project with a CHANGELOG gets one entry under its unreleased heading. Touch no code, no test, no spec and nothing in the knowledge base; keep each edit small. When nothing is wrong, change nothing and say so. End with one line per file you changed and why: the final review shows it.

steps.name: cover the group: write the test, or delete the unreachable lines
review the coverage test: assertions lens
steps.instructions: When the item's decision is delete: is the deleted code really unreachable? Look for callers, routes, reflection, configuration, scheduled jobs and event handlers that reach it; if anything can, that is blocking.

steps.name: walk the diff against the spec: name behaviour no criterion asks for
knowledge update
steps.instructions:
Update only these sections, and in them only the claims that cite the files listed (they changed since the last knowledge check). Re-read those files, fix or remove what is no longer true, add what this branch makes worth knowing, and keep every other line as it is. A section listed as not written yet is written from the code.
{{data.memory_plan.text}}

steps.name: ADR
steps.instructions: Write an ADR under docs/adr/NNNN-<title>.md (the next number) only for a decision this feature made that had a real alternative: Context (three sentences), Decision (present tense), Alternatives (and why they lost), Consequences (what gets easy, what gets hard). One per such decision. If nothing had a real alternative, write nothing and say so: an ADR that records the obvious approach is noise.

steps.name: edit the spec
steps.instructions: At the spec gate the user chose "{{data.spec_gate_answer.choice}}". edit: change only the criteria the note names (keep the ids of the others). rewrite: rewrite only the section the note names. Leave everything else as it is. The note: {{data.spec_gate_answer.why}}

steps.name: review the spec before approving
steps.instructions:
An adversarial read of the spec before it is approved (not of any code): criteria that are vague, untestable from outside, overlapping, or missing (an empty state, an error, an authorization rule, a limit); drawings that disagree with the criteria; a plan whose order breaks a dependency; a field name, format or limit of an outside API that the web research did not confirm (0.18.21: it belongs under Open questions). Do not edit anything. Spec: {{spec}}
The web research: {{data.web_docs_text}}

steps.name: criteria + plan + the review for the gate
move the criterion to the end
the amendment again with your note
spec amendment
steps.instructions:
The spec is frozen and approved, and it is wrong here: {{data.amend.reason}}
Read it again first: is the behaviour already there in other words, covered by another criterion, or out of scope? Only if none holds, append a dated block under "## Amendments" (never edit the frozen criteria in place): "### <date> — <criteria>", then "Was:" (the old wording, kept visible), "Now:", "Why:" (measured, not assumed). Under "Now:" write each changed criterion in full, one per line ("- **AC-n** [API] <new wording>"), or for a layer change only "tagged [API]" (or [WEB]); when the amendment is approved keel changes the criteria lines. A new criterion goes in the block with the next free id. For a criterion already done under the old wording, say whether it is reopened or ships under the old wording and why. REOPEN lists the done criteria to build again (or none); CONTRACT is yes when the outside surface (routes, schemas) changes.
